clarification.question: What should Claude vs. Groq optimize for?

goals.label: Best output quality
goals.hint: Reasoning, accuracy, and nuanced writing matter most

goals.label: Fastest responses
goals.hint: Low latency and snappy user experience come first

goals.label: Lowest cost at scale
goals.hint: Token pricing and high-volume economics drive the choice

options.name: Claude
options.tagline: Anthropic's model family built for careful reasoning and writing
pros: Strong at nuanced writing and complex instructions
cons: Higher per-token price at top tiers

options.name: Groq
options.tagline: Fast inference platform serving open-weight models on custom LPU hardware
pros: Low cost for supported open models
Good fit for real-time or streaming UX
cons: Output quality bounded by the hosted open models
Model choice is limited to what Groq hosts
Less depth on complex reasoning than frontier models

criteria.label: Output quality
criteria.rationale: Frontier Claude models lead on nuanced reasoning and writing

criteria.label: Reasoning depth
criteria.rationale: Claude handles multi-step complex tasks more reliably

criteria.label: Speed
criteria.rationale: Groq's LPU inference is far faster for token output

criteria.label: Cost efficiency
criteria.rationale: Groq's open-model pricing is typically lower per token

verdict.summary: For best output quality, Claude is the stronger choice, especially for complex reasoning and writing. Choose Groq only if speed matters more than top-tier answers and open-weight models are good enough.

options.name: Claude
options.tagline: Strong reasoning and writing via Anthropic's API
pros: Haiku tier is fast and affordable

options.name: Groq
options.tagline: Ultra-fast inference on custom LPU hardware
pros: Great for real-time and streaming UX

criteria.label: Raw speed
criteria.rationale: Groq's LPU hardware generates tokens far faster

criteria.label: First-token latency
criteria.rationale: Groq responds almost immediately; Claude takes longer to start

criteria.label: Output quality
criteria.rationale: Claude leads on reasoning and nuance; open models trail on hard tasks

criteria.label: Model choice
criteria.rationale: Claude offers tiers within one family; Groq hosts many open models

verdict.summary: For fastest responses, Groq is the clear winner, especially for real-time streaming. Choose Claude (Haiku tier) only if you need better quality at acceptable speed.

options.name: Claude
options.tagline: Premium model family from Anthropic with strong reasoning
pros: Good instruction following and safety defaults
Model tiers let you trade cost for capability
cons: Higher per-token cost than open-model hosts
Costs grow quickly at high volume

options.name: Groq
options.tagline: Fast inference hosting for open-weight models on LPU hardware
cons: Output quality varies by model choice

criteria.label: Cost per token
criteria.rationale: Groq hosts open models at lower per-token prices

criteria.label: Output quality
criteria.rationale: Claude leads on reasoning; open models trail on hard tasks

criteria.label: Speed
criteria.rationale: Groq's inference hardware delivers very low latency

criteria.label: Scale economics
criteria.rationale: Groq's pricing and throughput suit high request volumes

verdict.summary: For lowest cost at scale, Groq usually wins on price and throughput, provided an open-weight model meets your quality bar. Choose Claude if output quality justifies a higher per-token spend.
